# Turkey says Russia, Ukraine increasing attacks in Black Sea ahead of winter

By Tuvan Gumrukcu

ANKARA, Oct 8 (Reuters) – Intensifying attacks by Russia and Ukraine ahead of the winter are further endangering navigational safety in the Black Sea, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Thursday, adding ​that world powers must not allow the region to be turned ‌into a new front in the war.

NATO member Turkey, which has maintained good ties with both Moscow and Kyiv since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, has repeatedly called on both sides to halt attacks in the Black Sea that have also struck Turkish-flagged ‌and ​Turkish-owned commercial vessels. Ankara says it is awaiting ⁠responses to a proposal it ⁠conveyed to Russia and Ukraine aimed at stopping the attacks and ensuring the safe shipment of grain from the region.

Speaking at a joint press conference with his Hungarian counterpart Anita Orban in Ankara, Fidan said the attacks, ​which he described as a serious threat to the regional security, were getting worse even as Turkey had already proposed solutions.

Oct 8 (Reuters) - As Ukraine's capital came under some of the heaviest direct bombardment of the war last week, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy met a delegation of Japanese members of parliament and then German Chancellor ​Friedrich Merz.

While the Japanese parliamentarians visited an underground drone workshop in the capital, Merz attended a memorial to slain Ukrainian service personnel as well as the scene of a Russian strike on the National Academy of Sciences ‌in late September.

Sign up here.

Before Merz headed back to Berlin, the leaders announced that, despite warnings from the Kremlin for foreign embassies to quit the Ukrainian capital for safety, neither Germany nor any other major nation had any plans to do so.

Still, with a lack of air defences now leaving Kyiv and other major cities wide open to attack, and summer's warmth coming to an end, Ukrainians themselves are now bracing for perhaps the toughest winter of the 4-1/2-year-old war.

"Protection against all of this is the number one priority for me and Ukraine," Zelenskiy said, saying that Russian reverses on the eastern front were pushing a ​furious Kremlin towards throwing ever greater resources into its aerial onslaught.

# National Security Regulation & Investment Risk: Quarterly Update from Washington

![](/etc.clientlibs/dechert/clientlibs/clientlib-site/resources/images/loader.svg)

October 08, 2026

## Key Takeaways

* National security regulation is broadening, but not uniformly. This quarter combined expanded sanctions authorities and a proposed extension of FOCI review with targeted regulatory relief and efforts to make investment-security processes more efficient. The existing outbound investment rules remain operative while Treasury develops regulations implementing the COINS Act, but recent White House policy statements expressly contemplate broader restrictions.
* Companies should prepare for the possible implementation of BIS’s Affiliates Rule, scheduled to enter into effect on November 10, 2026, while monitoring whether BIS extends the current suspension. Recent reports suggest the Rule may be suspended for two additional months (until January 10, 2027).
* Enforcement continues to focus on known weaknesses and indirect channels. Treasury also brought the first enforcement action under the outbound investment regime, involving an unreported investment by a controlled foreign entity.
